newsitem.title: JAPAN: Fujita, Towa shares up on restructuring plan.
newsitem.headline: Fujita, Towa shares up on restructuring plan.

text.p: Shares of construction firm Fujita Corp and its group firm Towa Real Estate Development Co Ltd were bid-only on Monday morning, supported by a restructuring plan released by Fujita, traders said.
At 0036 GMT, Fujita's shares were up 13 yen at 103 yen. Meanwhile, Towa's shares were up 10 yen at 100 yen. Both issues were bid-only at the opening.
Fujita said on Monday it had formed a restructuring plan covering the period to March 31, 2000, and that its major creditor bank Sakura Bank Ltd had said it would accept the plan.
Under the restructuring programme, debt-ridden Fujita would try to cut its debts by 157.4 billion yen to 480 billion yen by the end of March 2000, a Fujita spokesman said.
It would also cut its work force by 560 workers to 4,900 during period through natural attrition, a halt of new recruitment and an early retirement programme, he said.
The company would also try to improve the profit margin of it construction projects to 10.1 percent in 1999/2000 from 8.9 percent in 1996/97, he said.
The spokesman said other banks, including Tokai Bank Ltd, were likely to accept the restructuring programme.
